Estimation of Generalized Linear Gaussian Process Models

Source: R/parameter_estimation.R
glgpm.Rd

Fits generalized linear Gaussian process models to spatial data, incorporating spatial Gaussian processes with a Matern correlation function. Supports Gaussian, binomial, Poisson and negative binomial response families.

Usage

glgpm(
  formula,
  data,
  family,
  invlink = NULL,
  denominator = NULL,
  distance_crs = NULL,
  distance_units = c("km", "m"),
  start_pars = NULL,
  fixed_pars = NULL,
  control_mcml = set_control_mcml(),
  control_mcmc = set_control_mcmc(),
  return_samples = TRUE,
  seed = NULL,
  messages = getOption("RiskMap.messages", TRUE)
)

Arguments

formula

A formula object specifying the model to be fitted. The formula should include fixed effects and spatial effects specified using gp() and optionally, random effects specified using re(). It can also include one offset() term that names a column of data, e.g. offset(log_exposure).

data

An sf object containing the variables in the model.

family

The distribution of the response given the random effects, with its link. Either one of the strings "gaussian", "binomial" and "poisson", which take the identity, logit and log links, a family object as in stats::glm(), such as binomial("probit"), or negative_binomial() for overdispersed counts with the log link, whose size is estimated unless it is held, by fixed_pars of glgpm() or by the family object MASS::negative.binomial(2). Where nothing is estimated, as in specify_glgpm(), the size must be given, as theta in its parameters. Binomial responses take the logit, probit, complementary log-log ("cloglog") and Cauchy ("cauchit") links, Poisson responses the log link and Gaussian responses the identity link. binomial("log") and poisson("identity") are not accepted, because they can give means outside the range of the family, nor is poisson("sqrt"), whose inverse gives the same mean to a positive and a negative linear predictor. Quasi-likelihood families, such as stats::quasibinomial(), have no likelihood to maximise and are not accepted either. Any other link can be given in invlink. A named link gives the same estimates as its inverse given in invlink, and is faster when that inverse cannot be differentiated symbolically, as for invlink = pnorm.

invlink

A function that maps the linear predictor to the mean of the response given the random effects, for a binomial or Poisson model whose link is not one of those that family names, such as a link for an imperfect diagnostic test. Its first and second derivatives are found symbolically where possible and numerically otherwise. They only steer the importance sampler, so they affect the speed of a fit and not its estimates. Not applicable for Gaussian models, and not to be combined with a family object that names a link other than logit or log. Custom links are experimental, and how they are given and checked may change in a minor release.

denominator

Optional denominator for binomial distributions, or exposure for Poisson and negative binomial ones, the mean of a count being the exposure times the inverse link of the linear predictor. Passed as a bare/unquoted column name present in data. If not provided, defaults to 1.

distance_crs

The projected coordinate reference system in which distances, and so phi, are measured, for example an EPSG code. data are transformed to it, and the model is fitted in it. The default, NULL, keeps projected data as they are and projects data in longitude and latitude to the CRS from propose_crs(), a UTM zone or a projection centred on the data, with a message naming the CRS and the units of distance. A CRS in longitude and latitude is refused. A warning of class riskmap_warning_crs is raised when the CRS used distorts distances by more than 1% over the data. variogram(), summarise_distance(), create_grid() and specify_glgpm() take the same argument, so that their distances can be measured as the fit's are.

distance_units

Character string, either "km" or "m", indicating the units used for internal coordinate distances and spatial parameters such as phi. The coordinates of the data keep the linear units of their CRS. Defaults to "km".

start_pars

NULL (the default), or a named list of starting values for any of the model's estimated parameters, one, several or all of them, named as in riskmap_parameters. beta is matched to the columns of the design matrix by name, or by position if it is unnamed and has a value for each, and sigma2_re to the re() terms in the same way. The flat names of unlist(coef(fit)), such as "beta.x", are accepted too, in a list or as that named vector, so start_pars = coef(fit) starts a fit from the estimates of another. Every other parameter takes its automatic start. glgpm_parameters() lists the parameters of a model before it is fitted.

fixed_pars

NULL (the default), or a named list of values at which to hold any of the model's parameters instead of estimating them, one, several or all of them, with the names and structure of start_pars. Every value must be finite, and every one but the coefficients positive, except the measurement error variance of a Gaussian model, which may be zero. A held coefficient enters the linear predictor as a known term, as an offset does. The other parameters are estimated with the held ones at their values, and with every parameter held the fit evaluates the likelihood at the values (exactly for a Gaussian model, by Monte Carlo on one sample for the others) and draws the conditional samples there, so that predict() works with given parameters. A parameter can't be both started and held, except that a start equal to its held value, as in start_pars = coef(fit) of a fit with the same holds, is left out. With one observation per location, a Gaussian model can estimate the nugget or the measurement error variance, not both, and a negative binomial model the nugget or the size, not both.

control_mcml

Control parameters for adaptive Monte Carlo maximum likelihood estimation. Must be returned by set_control_mcml().

control_mcmc

Control parameters for MCMC sampling for binomial or Poisson models. Must be an object of class RiskMap_control_mcmc as returned by set_control_mcmc().

return_samples

Logical indicating whether to draw and retain conditional samples at the fitted parameters. These samples are used to compute fitted values. If FALSE, final sampling is skipped and fitted values are not computed. Defaults to TRUE. Ignored for Gaussian models.

seed

Optional non-negative integer that seeds every random step of a binomial or Poisson fit: the Monte Carlo samples of the estimation and the final conditional samples. When NULL (the default), one integer is drawn from the session's random number generator, so set.seed() before the call also reproduces the fit. The seed used is returned as seed. The caller's random number state is otherwise left unchanged. Ignored for Gaussian models, which have no random step.

messages

Logical indicating whether to print messages, and a line for each stage of Monte Carlo maximum likelihood as described in riskmap_progress. Defaults to the option RiskMap.messages, or TRUE if it is not set.

Value

A fitted model of class RiskMap, a list. These components are part of its interface.

data

The sf data of the fit, in the CRS in which the model was fitted, so that distances between them are those that phi describes. sf::st_crs(fit$data) gives that CRS, and sf::st_transform(fit$data, fit$input_crs) gives the data in the CRS they were given in.

input_crs

The CRS of data as it was given.

formula

The model formula.

family

The name of the family, such as "binomial".

call

The matched call.

seed

The seed used for the random steps of a binomial, Poisson or negative binomial fit, whether given or drawn, so that glgpm(..., seed = fit$seed) reproduces the fit. NULL for Gaussian models.

distance_units

The units of distance, "km" or "m", in which phi is given.

The other components are internal and may change in any version of RiskMap. The estimates, their covariance and the likelihood are read with coef(), vcov(), logLik() and nobs(), fitted values with fitted(), standard errors and intervals with summary(), and how the fit was computed with check_fit().

Every result of RiskMap that can be saved and read again, such as a fit, a prediction or a profile, has the attribute riskmap_version, a list with the version of RiskMap that made it, as a package_version(), and sha, the commit it was installed from when it was installed from GitHub and NA otherwise. An object without it was made before RiskMap stamped its results, by an earlier version or an early development build of 2.0.0.

Details

Generalized linear Gaussian process models extend generalized linear models (GLMs) by incorporating spatial Gaussian processes to account for spatial correlation in the data. This function fits GLGPMs using maximum likelihood methods, allowing for Gaussian, binomial, Poisson and negative binomial response families. In the case of the binomial, Poisson and negative binomial families, a Monte Carlo maximum likelihood algorithm is used. A negative binomial model is fitted as the binomial model of its counts at each value of its size (see negative_binomial()).

The spatial Gaussian process is modeled with a Matern correlation function, which is flexible and commonly used in geostatistical modeling. The function supports both spatial covariates and unstructured random effects, providing a comprehensive framework to analyze spatially correlated data across different response distributions.

Additionally, the function allows for the inclusion of unstructured random effects, specified through the re() term in the model formula. These random effects can capture unexplained variability at specific locations beyond the fixed and spatial covariate effects, enhancing the model's flexibility in capturing complex spatial patterns.

The model is fitted in the projected CRS of distance_crs, or of data when it is NULL, and the data in longitude and latitude are projected to the CRS from propose_crs() with a message. The distance_units argument controls whether distances between locations (and so parameters such as phi) are expressed in kilometers ("km", the default) or meters ("m").

The control_mcmc argument specifies the control parameters for MCMC sampling. This argument must be an object returned by set_control_mcmc(). Non-Gaussian models are fitted by certified Monte Carlo maximum likelihood (MCML), controlled by control_mcml (see set_control_mcml()). The estimate is corrected with an independent validation sample and certified with a second, fresh one, which bounds its Monte Carlo error in statistical standard errors, with an allowance for that sample's own error taken from it and from a replicate of it (see set_control_mcml()). The samples are enlarged only when the certificate exceeds the tolerance, and a warning is issued if the tolerance is not met within the configured limits. check_fit() reports every stage. Warnings are kept for what changes how a result is read, and check_fit() goes through all the checks on the computation, with what to do about any that need a look. The estimation samples and the final conditional samples are drawn from separate streams derived from seed, so glgpm(..., seed = fit$seed) reproduces a fit exactly.

Parameters not given in start_pars take RiskMap's defaults, which are the coefficients of the regression without latent effects and phi at the 10th percentile of the distances between locations. In a Gaussian model every variance, that of the spatial process, of an estimated nugget, of the measurement error and of each re() term, starts at the variance of the residuals of that regression, and the model is fitted to those residuals divided by their standard deviation, so that a fit does not depend on the units of the response. In the other models the variances start at 1, and the size of a negative binomial model at that of the regression without latent effects. A binomial, Poisson or negative binomial model with the canonical link and without re() terms compares the defaults with the estimates of a Gaussian model fitted to the empirical link of the data (the empirical logit of a binomial model), with one observation per location, the totals of the location where it has several records, and starts from the one with the higher Laplace approximation of the likelihood. The values given in start_pars replace their own in both, and set_control_mcml(start_comparison = FALSE) skips the comparison. A start of phi far from the distances between the locations, below a hundredth of the smallest or above ten times the largest, gives a warning, since it may be in other units. summary.RiskMap() says which starting values a fit used and why.

stats::update() refits a model with some of its arguments changed, as in update(fit, . ~ . + elevation) or update(fit, fixed_pars = list(phi = 20)). It evaluates the call again, with the data it names in the environment where update() is called.

See also

The methods for a fit are print(), summary(), coef(), fitted(), logLik() with vcov() and nobs(), predict(), profile() and to_table(). check_fit(), plot_mcmc(), summarise_mcmc(), parametric_bootstrap(), assess_prediction() and assess_extrapolation() take a fit too. glgpm_parameters() lists the parameters of a model before it is fitted, and set_control_mcml() and set_control_mcmc() set how it is fitted.

Examples


data(italy_sim)

# intercept only
fit <- glgpm(
  formula = y ~ gp(),
  data = italy_sim[1:100,],
  family = "gaussian",
  messages = FALSE
)

summary(fit)
#> ── Linear geostatistical model ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> glgpm(formula = y ~ gp(), data = italy_sim[1:100, ], family = "gaussian",
#>     messages = FALSE)
#> The identity link.
#> The limits are those of 95% confidence intervals.
#> 
#> Regression coefficients
#>             Estimate Lower limit Upper limit   StdErr z.value   p.value    
#> (Intercept)  9.32340     7.70078    10.94603  0.82788  11.262 < 2.2e-16 ***
#> ---
#> Signif. codes:  0 ‘***’ 0.001 ‘**’ 0.01 ‘*’ 0.05 ‘.’ 0.1 ‘ ’ 1
#> 
#> Measurement error
#>                        Estimate Lower limit Upper limit
#> Measurement error var.  0.17859     0.13335      0.2392
#> 
#> Spatial Gaussian process, Matern correlation with kappa = 0.5
#>                          Estimate Lower limit Upper limit
#> Spatial process var.       4.8494      1.8196      12.924
#> Spatial corr. scale (km)  39.0150      2.7773     548.084
#> Variance of the nugget effect fixed at 0
#> 
#> Log-likelihood   8.618636
#> AIC             -9.237272

# add a covariate
fit <- update(fit, . ~ . + pop_dens)

summary(fit)
#> ── Linear geostatistical model ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> glgpm(formula = y ~ gp() + pop_dens, data = italy_sim[1:100,
#>     ], family = "gaussian", messages = FALSE)
#> The identity link.
#> The limits are those of 95% confidence intervals.
#> 
#> Regression coefficients
#>               Estimate Lower limit Upper limit     StdErr z.value   p.value    
#> (Intercept) 7.70187620  6.37937916  9.02437323 0.67475578 11.4143 < 2.2e-16 ***
#> pop_dens    0.00046825  0.00023917  0.00069733 0.00011688  4.0063 6.168e-05 ***
#> ---
#> Signif. codes:  0 ‘***’ 0.001 ‘**’ 0.01 ‘*’ 0.05 ‘.’ 0.1 ‘ ’ 1
#> 
#> Measurement error
#>                        Estimate Lower limit Upper limit
#> Measurement error var.  0.17853     0.13331      0.2391
#> 
#> Spatial Gaussian process, Matern correlation with kappa = 0.5
#>                          Estimate Lower limit Upper limit
#> Spatial process var.      1.77451     0.59997      5.2484
#> Spatial corr. scale (km) 75.04610     9.01027    625.0556
#> Variance of the nugget effect fixed at 0
#> 
#> Log-likelihood   14.34117
#> AIC             -18.68233

# add a random effect
fit <- glgpm(
  formula = y ~ gp() + re(province),
  data = italy_sim[1:100,],
  family = "gaussian",
  messages = FALSE
)

summary(fit)
#> ── Linear geostatistical model ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> glgpm(formula = y ~ gp() + re(province), data = italy_sim[1:100,
#>     ], family = "gaussian", messages = FALSE)
#> The identity link.
#> The limits are those of 95% confidence intervals.
#> 
#> Regression coefficients
#>             Estimate Lower limit Upper limit   StdErr z.value   p.value    
#> (Intercept)  9.34077     7.92351    10.75804  0.72311  12.918 < 2.2e-16 ***
#> ---
#> Signif. codes:  0 ‘***’ 0.001 ‘**’ 0.01 ‘*’ 0.05 ‘.’ 0.1 ‘ ’ 1
#> 
#> Measurement error
#>                        Estimate Lower limit Upper limit
#> Measurement error var.  0.17859     0.13335      0.2392
#> 
#> Spatial Gaussian process, Matern correlation with kappa = 0.5
#>                          Estimate Lower limit Upper limit
#> Spatial process var.     0.438837    0.022556      8.5376
#> Spatial corr. scale (km) 1.054947    0.000000         Inf
#> Variance of the nugget effect fixed at 0
#> 
#> Unstructured random effects
#>                             Estimate Lower limit Upper limit
#> province (random eff. var.)   4.2742      1.4733        12.4
#> 
#> Log-likelihood   9.082286
#> AIC             -8.164572

# estimate the nugget
fit <- glgpm(
  formula = y ~ gp(nugget = TRUE),
  data = italy_sim[1:100,],
  family = "gaussian",
  messages = FALSE
)

summary(fit)
#> ── Linear geostatistical model ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> glgpm(formula = y ~ gp(nugget = TRUE), data = italy_sim[1:100,
#>     ], family = "gaussian", messages = FALSE)
#> The identity link.
#> The limits are those of 95% confidence intervals.
#> 
#> Regression coefficients
#>             Estimate Lower limit Upper limit   StdErr z.value   p.value    
#> (Intercept)  9.32340     7.70078    10.94603  0.82788  11.262 < 2.2e-16 ***
#> ---
#> Signif. codes:  0 ‘***’ 0.001 ‘**’ 0.01 ‘*’ 0.05 ‘.’ 0.1 ‘ ’ 1
#> 
#> Measurement error
#>                        Estimate Lower limit Upper limit
#> Measurement error var.  0.17859     0.13335      0.2392
#> 
#> Spatial Gaussian process, Matern correlation with kappa = 0.5
#>                            Estimate Lower limit Upper limit
#> Spatial process var.     4.8494e+00  1.8196e+00      12.924
#> Spatial corr. scale (km) 3.9015e+01  2.7773e+00     548.085
#> Variance of the nugget   4.2815e-07  0.0000e+00         Inf
#> 
#> Log-likelihood   8.618636
#> AIC             -7.237272

# binomial model
data(loaloa)

# reduce iterations to speed up the fit, and set a
# seed for reproducibility
control_mcmc <- set_control_mcmc(n_draws = 8,
                                 burnin = 20)

fit <- glgpm(NO_INF ~ gp(),
             data = loaloa[1:50,],
             denominator = NO_EXAM,
             family = "binomial",
             control_mcmc = control_mcmc,
             seed = 42,
             messages = FALSE)
#> ℹ `data` are in longitude and latitude, so they are projected to a custom
#>   oblique Mercator projection ("RiskMap oblique Mercator 11.5E 5N azimuth -72.5
#>   k0 0.9998") for fitting, with distances in km. No UTM zone keeps distances
#>   within 0.5% over them. Set `distance_crs` to choose the projection.

summary(fit)
#> ── Binomial geostatistical model ───────────────────────────────────────────────
#> glgpm(formula = NO_INF ~ gp(), data = loaloa[1:50, ], family = "binomial",
#>     denominator = NO_EXAM, control_mcmc = control_mcmc, seed = 42,
#>     messages = FALSE)
#> The canonical logit link.
#> The limits are those of 95% confidence intervals.
#> 
#> Regression coefficients
#>             Estimate Lower limit Upper limit  StdErr z.value   p.value    
#> (Intercept)  -2.1233     -3.2385     -1.0081  0.5690 -3.7317 0.0001902 ***
#> ---
#> Signif. codes:  0 ‘***’ 0.001 ‘**’ 0.01 ‘*’ 0.05 ‘.’ 0.1 ‘ ’ 1
#> 
#> Spatial Gaussian process, Matern correlation with kappa = 0.5
#>                          Estimate Lower limit Upper limit
#> Spatial process var.       2.1220      0.9347      4.8173
#> Spatial corr. scale (km) 102.1364     34.7202    300.4544
#> Variance of the nugget effect fixed at 0
#> 
#> Log-likelihood  -2018.33
#> 
#> Monte Carlo maximum likelihood
#> ✔ Certified. The Monte Carlo error of the estimate is within 0.0055 statistical
#>   standard errors (an approximate 95% bound, tolerance 0.1).
#> ℹ The starting values came from a Gaussian fit to the transformed data, which
#>   the Laplace approximation of the likelihood preferred to RiskMap's defaults.
#> ✔ No check needs a look. See `check_fit()` for the details.
